Elaine Kim: Heads-up — I'm about to merge the docs PR that changes the model-routing example (PR #482). Before I do, can someone from runtime confirm a couple of blocking details?

Elaine Kim: The example says we 'fall back to a compatible variant' but doesn't say what happens to the KV cache or quantization mismatch. That bit matters for the migration note.

Elaine Kim: Current example YAML in the PR: ```yaml
routing:
  policy: latency
  fallback_order: [fast-7b, fast-7b-quant]
  preserve_kv_cache: false # <-- is this the true default?
  canary_grace_secs: 20
```

Elaine Kim: If preserve_kv_cache is false by default, we should explicitly call it out in the docs and show the latency implication. If it's true for some cases, we need to state the exact rules. Please advise so I don't merge incorrect guidance. @Samir / @Matt

Samir Patel: Short answer: default depends on variant compatibility.

Samir Patel: If the fallback variant is architecture-compatible (same model family & tokenizer) we keep the KV cache. If it differs only by quantization but binary-compatible, we also try to preserve KV where possible. If tokenization or vocab differs, we drop cache.

Samir Patel: We don't have a single boolean global default that fits all cases. Runtime checks three things: arch, tokenizer_id, and KV-serialization-compat. If any check fails -> preserve_kv_cache=false.

Matt O'Rourke: To add: when preserve_kv_cache=false you'll see an immediate latency spike for the first few tokens on fallback (cold KV). We should show a small trace example in the docs.

Elaine Kim: That's helpful. Can you give the exact behavior we should document (one short paragraph + a tiny example)? I can draft text and add to the PR.

Samir Patel: Doc text suggestion: "When a request is routed to a fallback model, the runtime attempts to reuse the caller's KV cache if the fallback is binary- and tokenizer-compatible. If compatibility checks fail, the runtime starts the fallback without cached state, which can add a cold-start token latency penalty for the next request."

Samir Patel: Example latency note: "Observed: +120–300ms on first generation token when KV is dropped for 8k context workloads on A100."

Matt O'Rourke: Also call out quantized variants: even if quantization differs, we usually preserve KV for same-arch builds, but output probabilities can differ slightly. Recommend adding: "Verify outputs with your eval prompts after enabling fallback."

Elaine Kim: OK — I'll add that text plus a tiny YAML snippet showing `preserve_kv_cache: false` as an explicit opt-out example.

Docsbot: CI / docs-preview: linkcheck failed for PR #482 — broken link to runtime config reference at /docs/runtime/routing/config — please fix.

Elaine Kim: Thanks Docsbot. I will drop the merge until the runtime confirm and linkcheck are fixed. Marking PR as WIP.

Samir Patel: I'll file a tiny runtime docs note in the reference page and ping you when it's up. ETA ~2 hours.

Matt O'Rourke: If you want a quick interim sentence, add: "Fallback may drop cached state; see runtime routing reference for compatibility rules (link pending)." We can update link after Samir's note lands.

Elaine Kim: Perfect. I'll push an update with that placeholder and the example. Hold merge until Samir confirms link and we get a green linkcheck. :thumbsup:
